claim: Leaderboard renders a broken avatar with no onerror fallback

db_evidence.note: Row created 2026-08-28, ~3 weeks BEFORE this audit (2026-09-22) -> NOT a probe artefact of this sweep. Only 1 of 72 users has a bad URL; 0 have null/empty, so this is stale test data, not an empty-value code path.

api_evidence.request: GET http://localhost:8080/api/leaderboard?page=0&size=20 (Bearer student token, rate-limit buckets flushed first)
api_evidence.row_position: rank 5, page 1 of 4 -> visible without any paging trickery

url_evidence.curl_head: HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found (Content-Type: text/html, cloudflare, body = 'Example Domain' HTML)
url_evidence.note: The host returns 404 text/html, so Chromium blocks the response as an image: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB.

live_dom_evidence.tool: Chrome DevTools MCP evaluate_script on http://localhost:5173/leaderboard
live_dom_evidence.screenshot: skeptic2-v13-leaderboard-broken-avatar.png (rank 5 shows the browser broken-image glyph with 'Ảnh' alt text in the 48x48 slot)

source_evidence.root_cause_confirmed: The `||` fallback only fires for null/empty/undefined. A non-empty but dead URL is truthy, so the dicebear fallback never applies. There is no @error/onerror handler on this img (grep: none in Leaderboard.vue, none in components/common/, no global handler in main.js or App.vue).
source_evidence.note_on_pattern: The project already uses an @error image-fallback pattern in two other views; Leaderboard.vue's omission is an inconsistency/gap, not a deliberate design choice.

refutation_attempts.result: NO. Row created 2026-08-28, 3 weeks before the audit. Rate-limit buckets were flushed before the HTTP batch; API returned 200. The broken request is a cross-origin image fetch to example.com, unrelated to the API rate limiter.
NO. This is an image naturalWidth==0 check plus a real network failure (ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB), not an overflow measurement. Screenshot visually confirms the broken glyph.
NO. /leaderboard rendered 20 article rows and 72 total users; page is the real leaderboard, not a login redirect.

refutation_attempts.attempt: Is this correct browser behaviour rather than a bug?
refutation_attempts.result: PARTIALLY. Rendering alt text on a failed image is standard browser behaviour, and the alt text is meaningful, so this is NOT an a11y failure. But a user-visible broken-image glyph on a ranking row is a genuine (minor) UI defect, and the component has no robustness against a URL that later 404s (e.g. a deleted Cloudinary asset). The claim is a legitimate LOW.

refutation_attempts.attempt: Is it only bad data, not a code defect?
refutation_attempts.result: The trigger is stale test data (1 of 72 users), so the report's fix should include cleaning the row; but the missing @error fallback is a real gap the claim correctly identifies. The claim itself already says 'add @error and/or clean the row', so it does not overstate the code defect.

conclusion: Confirmed by real DB row, real HTTP 200 payload, real DOM (naturalWidth 0), real network failure (ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB) and a screenshot. Not a probe artefact; the row predates the audit. The claimed LOW severity is justified: cosmetic, one row of 72, alt text still present, functionality unaffected. No severity correction.
